removed.reason: ralston1872:p.146 does say the Saratof Rusalkas 'are described as hideous', but 'hideous' is an evaluative style word, which appearance may not hold even where the source uses it (as v1 cut 'hideous' from baba-yaga); the clause is only that word, so it is removed. The physical details on the same page (humpbacked, hairy, sharp claws, iron hook) are kept as their own clauses (1d-c fix round, reviewer finding).

downgraded.text: Carries an iron hook with which it tries to seize passers-by.
downgraded.reason: Trying to seize passers-by is behaviour, not physical description, and is misplaced in appearance (belongs in behavior_habitat); 'carries' narrowed to the page's plain 'with ... an iron hook'.

retagged.text: They sit on the mill-wheel and turn round with it amid the splash of the stream.
retagged.reason: Machal p.255 has them sit on the mill-wheel splashing each other but not turn round with it; Afanasyev p.123 has them sit on the mill-wheel, turn with it and admire the spray, and Ralston p.140 has them cling to it and turn round amid the splash.

retagged.text: In Little-Russia shifts, rags and skeins of thread are hung on oaks and other trees before Whitsuntide as presents to the Rusalkas.
retagged.reason: Machal p.254 says women hang linen strips on branches but does not place it in Little-Russia; Ralston p.141 supports the clause as worded.

flagged.reason: Afanasyev p.125 gives the name only for the Kharkov Government, in an OCR-split instrumental form ('лоско талкою'); the Ukrainians attribution rests on the preceding sentence about the Little Russians, not on a direct statement.

grade_rationale.text: Ralston records the Rusalkas for Russia and, by region, for Little-Russia, the Ukraine and White-Russia.
Machal says belief in the Rusalky is most widely spread among the Russians.
Afanasyev records rusalki 'among us and the Czechs' and says peasants people rivers, springs, lakes and seas with them.

Ralston's Rusalka account cites Afanasyev in footnotes for the tickling etymology and the Rusalka-week grave offering, so those passages are not independent of him; his other Rusalka passages carry no such citation and count as independent.
Machal's Rusalky pages cite no source, so he is counted as a third author, although his mill-wheel 'Kuku' detail matches Afanasyev's wording closely.
Three authors (Afanasyev, Ralston, Machal) and four peoples (Russians, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Czechs) support the verified entry; the Czech row rests on one line of Afanasyev.
